stage1.impression: A clean, legible night composition: the tilted ring globe reads at once against a dark canal, and the hard spot's coloured shadow on the paving is the most photographic idea in the frame. But it reads as CG. The houses are untextured brown boxes with flat, evenly glowing window cards (several near-white), the paving is a clean tiled texture, the bollards and two odd posts in front of the facade look like primitives, and an amber cast over everything washes the six colours toward pastel. A jury would see a specific, striking object, but in a generic rendered street rather than on a real Amsterdam canal.

blocking_9: The houses across the canal read as real Amsterdam brick canal houses: brick texture with mortar and staining, varied gables, window frames with depth, curtains and varied warm interiors behind the glass, no flat uniform window cards
The lit windows sit below the globe in brightness: no window's lum_median above about 120, and no neutral or blue-white windows

The six rim colours read saturated and distinct (the orange meridian orange rather than peach, the violet violet rather than lavender-blue), with the scene's amber cast reduced so the globe is the frame's only saturated colour
The quay reads as worn Amsterdam clinker brick and a stone kerb, with variation, joints and damp sheen, not a clean tiled plane
The water carries long, broken reflections of the rims and windows
Some sign of life and scale: a parked bicycle, a far figure, a railing or a moored boat
Grain and denoise read as a camera's: no mottled denoiser blotches in the facade's flat areas

defects.what: Facades are flat untextured brown planes with repeated identical window modules; reads as a blockout model, not brick canal houses
Lit windows are flat emissive cards (lum_range 7.9 inside one window), several near-white or bluish-grey (one measured RGB 119/121/124), brighter than the globe's own glass
Two tall dark posts stand in front of the facade with sliced tops; they read as stray geometry floating over the water
Bollards are smooth glossy reddish cylinders, plastic-looking, with no cap or patina
Paving is a clean, regular, CG-looking tile grid with no joints in relief, wear or damp sheen; no stone kerb at the quay edge
Rims are thin and the colours are washed toward pastel by the amber grade: the orange meridian reads peach, the violet reads periwinkle; the clear faces show almost nothing
Global amber cast: b_median 5 to 16 across the facade, paving and water; the whole frame is one orange-brown
Water reflections are short and blurred; the rims barely reflect in the canal
The plinth is a smooth matte black cylinder with no blackened-steel sheen, edge highlight or patina
Mottled low-frequency denoiser noise on the flat facade
No sign of life or scale: no people, no bicycle, no boats

changes.problem: The houses across the canal read as a blockout: flat brown planes with repeated, identical window cards.

evidence.measured: facade lum_median 20.7 on a flat, untextured surface; one lit window measures lum_range 7.9, a uniform card

change.setting: the materials' finish of the houses (brick)
change.from: flat brown shader, emissive window cards
change.to: dark Amsterdam brick with mortar joints and bump, faint staining and variation from house to house; recessed white-painted frames with sash bars; windows given interior depth (a parallax or box interior, curtains, a lamp) rather than an emissive plane; vary the gable shapes and heights

changes.expected: The far bank reads as real canal houses; lit windows show varied warm interiors with internal gradients

changes.problem: The lit windows are too bright and too neutral or cold, so they compete with the globe for attention.

evidence.measured: lum_median 181.6, RGB 194/179/171; another at 975,130 is neutral grey 119/121/124

change.setting: the houses across: windows lit and their glow
change.from: 0.35 lit, glow 0.08, some white or blue-white
change.to: 0.25 lit, glow 0.035, all warm 2400 to 2900 K with variation, none white

changes.expected: Windows become warm, dim accents; the globe is the brightest element apart from the street lamp

changes.problem: An amber cast over the whole frame drains the six rim colours toward pastel and makes the scene monochrome orange.

evidence.measured: paving RGB median 93/53/31; facade b_median 5; the globe region's own median is 44/24/8

change.to: 2900 (lamps stay warm but cleaner; neutrals become warm grey rather than orange)

changes.expected: The paving and facade move toward warm grey-brown; the rim colours separate and saturate against them

changes.problem: The rims are thin and dim relative to the windows, so the globe does not dominate and the colours read pastel.

evidence.measured: globe region lum_median 27.0, p95 185; windows across reach 181

change.to: 0.35, checking that the cores do not clip to white (keep each hue's saturation); let a soft bloom or halation in post spread about 3 px

changes.expected: The rims are the brightest saturated element and each hue holds its colour at the core

changes.problem: The quay paving is a clean CG tile grid with no kerb, wear or dampness.

evidence.measured: lum_range 69 with a smooth, even texture and regular tiles at 1:1

change.setting: the materials' finish of the quay (paving, stone kerb)
change.to: Amsterdam clinker brick in a herringbone or stretcher bond with recessed joints, colour variation per brick, a damp low-roughness sheen (roughness 0.35 to 0.5) catching the spot and the lamp; a grey granite kerb with a rounded edge at the water

changes.expected: The ground reads at real scale; the coloured shadow and the lamp leave soft specular streaks on the bricks

changes.problem: The canal shows only short, soft reflections and almost none of the globe.

evidence.measured: lum_median 19.3, p95 79.5; the rims are not visible in the water

change.to: glossier water (roughness near 0.02) with a finer, lower-amplitude ripple so the reflections of the windows, lamp and rims stretch into long, broken vertical streaks

changes.expected: Coloured streaks from the rims and warm streaks from the windows appear in the water, which ties the work to the canal

changes.problem: Primitive-looking props (glossy red bollards, two sliced posts in front of the facade) and no sign of life.

evidence.measured: bollards are smooth saturated red-brown cylinders (r 46, b 6) competing with the globe's colour; the posts at x 750 and 970 have sliced tops

change.from: plain cylinder bollards, two bare posts
change.to: black cast-iron Amsterdammertje bollards with the triple-X relief; remove the two posts or make them proper canal-side lamp posts; add a parked bicycle against a railing, one or two far figures on the opposite quay, and a moored boat

changes.expected: The site reads as Amsterdam and gives the 2 m globe a human scale; no saturated colour other than the globe

changes.problem: The plinth reads as a matte black CG cylinder rather than blackened steel.

evidence.measured: lum_median 9.7, p95 93, no edge highlight on the top arris

change.to: blackened steel with a soft uneven sheen (roughness 0.3 to 0.5 varied), a brownish patina, a crisp highlight on the top edge from the spot and coloured reflections of the rims on its top face

changes.expected: The plinth reads as heavy metal with a sharp edge, and carries coloured reflections of the globe

out_of_scope.request: Thicker rim profile or more visible clear faces on the discs so the globe reads as solid acrylic rather than neon hoops
out_of_scope.why: The 25 mm discs, rim-lit with clear faces, are fixed by the card

out_of_scope.request: The violet meridian reads as lavender-blue and the orange as peach
out_of_scope.why: The disc colours are fixed; only the grade and white balance (c3) may correct how they read
